description: A worked calibration set: twelve candidate outputs and the grades a careful author gave them, spanning the scale. Grading twelve samples is a real sitting, and this set exists so a fresh install can show the whole calibration path without one.

The Halden works modernised its reconciliation in March 2026, replacing a four-hour overnight batch with a 38-minute incremental run. The change was written by Ingrid Sorensen over a fortnight, drawing on eleven years of running the process she replaced. The new run surfaced 213 discrepancies in its first month; nine were genuine stock errors and the rest were artefacts of the system it retired.
In March 2026 Halden switched to incremental reconciliation, cutting the run from 4 hours 20 minutes to 38 minutes, and saving the company roughly 400,000 euros a year.

The reconciliation at the Halden works now runs incrementally rather than overnight, a change made in March 2026 by Ingrid Sorensen. It finishes in 38 minutes rather than 4 hours 20, and in its first month it found 213 discrepancies of which nine mattered.
Halden changed how it reconciles stock, which is faster now, and the person who did it had done the old one for a long time, and there were a lot of discrepancies but not many real ones.

reference_jury.description: A deterministic jury that reproduces the author's own grade with an alternating one-point scatter. It is not a model; it exists so a shipped calibration set has a figure that can be reproduced exactly on any machine, with no GPU and no network.
